must_contain.claim: ValidationInfo exposes field_name but not the field's type/annotation or owning model

question: Since Vitest browser mode has no Playwright-style storageState/auth.setup.ts, what's the right pattern to log in once and share the session/token across test files?
landing_rule_applied: no doc link in accepted answer -> nav/title match: 'Browser Mode' guide page, matching 'browser mode' in the question title

facts.fact: Browser mode runs test code natively inside the browser (not Node), which is why there's no Node-side context object to save/restore like Playwright's storageState
facts.quote: run your tests in the browser natively, providing access to browser globals

facts.fact: globalSetup runs once in the main process before test workers are created (so it's the right place to do a real login)
facts.quote: global setup is called before the test workers are created

facts.fact: Data from globalSetup is passed into tests via provide()/inject(), and must be serializable since it crosses processes
facts.quote: Define values that can be accessed inside your tests using inject method

facts.fact: setupFiles (as opposed to globalSetup) run in the same process as each test file, which is where browser-side code (e.g. localStorage.setItem) belongs
facts.quote: setup files are executed in the same process as tests, unlike globalSetup

notes: guide/browser/ sits in the docs' 'Guide' sidebar section (prev=guide/browser/why, next=guide/browser/multiple-setups per the VitePress sidebar config); config/globalsetup, config/provide, config/setupfiles sit in the separate 'Config' section. None of the 3 needed config pages is adjacent to the landing page. (The 3 config pages are themselves mutually adjacent in the sidebar: setupfiles -> provide -> globalsetup.) Judgement call: verifying vitest.dev directly was not possible by curl alone (VitePress 2.0-alpha renders content client-side); I verified facts against the docs' own markdown source in the vitest-dev/vitest GitHub repo (docs/config/*.md, docs/guide/browser/index.md), which is the source of truth the site is built from.

must_contain.claim: Do the real login once in globalSetup (runs once in Node before workers), not per test file
must_contain.quote: global setup is called before the test workers are created

must_contain.claim: Pass the token from globalSetup to tests via project.provide(...) / inject(...)
must_contain.quote: Define values that can be accessed inside your tests using inject method

must_contain.claim: Put the browser-side code that consumes the token (e.g. localStorage.setItem) in setupFiles, which runs in-process with each test file
must_contain.quote: setup files are executed in the same process as tests, unlike globalSetup

wrong.claim: Recommending a Playwright-style storageState file / auth.setup.ts for Vitest browser mode
wrong.why_wrong: browser mode has no Node-side context object to persist that way; test code runs in the browser itself

wrong.claim: Claiming globalSetup runs once per test file
wrong.why_wrong: docs state it runs once before any worker is created, not per file

check: Implement the globalSetup + provide + setupFiles pattern and assert inject('authToken') returns the expected token inside a browser-mode test.

question: Why does a custom plugin that wraps @docusaurus/plugin-content-docs and re-exports its lifecycle methods (like configureWebpack) throw errors about missing/undefined option defaults, and how is it fixed?
landing_rule_applied: no doc link in accepted answer -> nav/title match: question names 'configureWebpack function' explicitly, which is documented on the 'Lifecycle APIs' reference page

facts.fact: configureWebpack modifies the internal webpack config passed in by Docusaurus
facts.quote: Modifies the internal webpack config

facts.fact: validateOptions returns validated and normalized plugin options and is called before the plugin is initialized (must be forwarded from a wrapped plugin, or option defaults stay undefined)
facts.quote: Returns validated and normalized options for the plugin

notes: Both pages are in the same 'Plugin Methods' API reference section, but static-methods' own pager is prev=i18n-lifecycles / next=plugins, and lifecycle-apis' pager is prev=plugin-methods(README) / next=extend-infrastructure -- several pages apart, not adjacent. Judgement call: the accepted answer gave no doc link at all; it stated a source-level fact (forward validateOptions or options stay unnormalized) which I confirmed is documented, but is documented on a different reference page than the one the question's own wording (configureWebpack) points to.

must_contain.claim: A wrapper plugin must re-export/forward validateOptions from the wrapped plugin, or its option defaults never get normalized
must_contain.quote: Returns validated and normalized options for the plugin

wrong.claim: The fix is to re-implement or tweak configureWebpack itself
wrong.why_wrong: configureWebpack only shapes the webpack config; the missing piece is forwarding validateOptions, a separate static method

must_contain.quote: Whether to enable the unstable preview style formatting

question: Is there a better way than listing the same documents in two toctree directives (one shallow, one deep) to avoid the 'referenced in multiple toctrees' warning?

facts.quote: it generates "next chapter", "previous chapter" and "parent chapter" links

facts.fact: :doc: links directly to a document by name and, with no explicit link text, uses that document's own title as the caption -- letting you build a plain link list without adding a second toctree hierarchy
facts.quote: the link caption will be the title of the given document

notes: Both pages are under the docs' broader 'usage/' section, but directives.html's own rel=prev/next (checked via <link> tags in the fetched HTML) is roles.html/field-lists.html -- referencing.html is neither, so it's same-section-nonadjacent rather than adjacent. This task is a clean illustration of mdflow's exact use case: Sphinx's own doc pages literally carry rel=prev/next <link> tags in their HTML head.

must_contain.claim: toctree defines document hierarchy (parent/child), which is why the same warning includes ['index','index'] when documents are listed twice
must_contain.quote: it generates "next chapter", "previous chapter" and "parent chapter" links

must_contain.claim: Use :doc: for a plain, non-hierarchy link list; it will use the target document's own title automatically
must_contain.quote: the link caption will be the title of the given document

wrong.claim: Claiming a document can be listed in two real toctree directives with no consequence
wrong.why_wrong: docs describe toctree as defining a single document hierarchy, which is exactly why duplicate listing triggers the warning

check: Build a small Sphinx project using one real toctree (detailed) plus :doc: links (short list) and confirm the 'referenced in multiple toctrees' warning no longer appears in the build log.

question: Why doesn't a cookie set with setSignedCookie() show up in the browser when the handler returns the response from c.env.ASSETS.fetch()?

must_contain.quote: You can access the Response object that will be returned

question: What's the biome-ignore comment syntax to suppress a lint rule that comes from a GritQL plugin, rather than a built-in rule?
